2017_110_071817mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of July 18, 2017 at the Services Building. Its central action is a resolution placing a building and site sinking fund tax proposal on the ballot at a special school election on November 7, 2017 — one mill for ten years, July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028, estimated to raise approximately $3,745,257 in the 2018 calendar year. The packet also extends Superintendent Richard Machesky's contract through June 30, 2020 after a third consecutive HIGHLY EFFECTIVE evaluation, extends the contracts of the deputy and assistant superintendents and some forty administrators, renews MHSAA membership, and awards $107,567.40 of middle school furniture and a $129,297.64 sound system replacement.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, July 18, 2017, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Agenda: Pledge; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; General – Consent Agenda (six sets of June minutes); Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda); Other; Adjournment.

**8.A — Building and site sinking fund on the November ballot**
The Board resolves to ask voters for a building and site sinking fund tax of one mill annually for ten years, from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028, at a special school election on November 7, 2017, and authorizes the Superintendent or designee to certify the ballot language to the Election Coordinator no later than 4:00 p.m. on August 15, 2017. The ballot text explains that proceeds must be audited and cannot be used for teacher, administrator or employee salaries, maintenance or other operating expenses, and may go to purchasing real estate for sites, constructing or repairing school buildings, school security improvements, and acquiring or upgrading technology. One mill is $1.00 per $1,000 of taxable valuation, estimated to provide approximately $3,745,257 during the 2018 calendar year.

A draft campaign timeline accompanies it, running from April vendor outreach through an August 1 petition filing, the August 15 ballot certification, a September 8 School Life kickoff issue, a September 15 informational mailer, an October 10 registration deadline, an October 15 podcast and an October 16 mailer to district homes, to the November 7 election.

**Personnel**
6.A extends Dr. Machesky's contract from July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2020. The Board's published assessment records that he has completed his third year as a HIGHLY EFFECTIVE superintendent, meeting or exceeding expectations in all evaluation categories, with a vision that is data-based and collaborative. 6.B extends one-year successor contracts for Mark Dziatczak (Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning), Rick West (Business Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Jordan Harris (Employee Services) through June 30, 2019. 6.C extends the contracts of some forty administrators through June 30, 2019 — every principal and assistant principal in the district plus seven directors, among them Lara Dixon at Athens, Remo Roncone at Troy High, Audra Melton at Baker, Brian Zawislak as an assistant principal at Troy High, and directors Kerry Birmingham, Rob Carson, Jennifer Gottlieb, Michael Jolly, David Pass, Christin Silagy and Stephanie Trotter.

**Curriculum and remaining business**
7.A enrolls the district's six secondary schools in the Michigan High School Athletic Association for August 1, 2017 through July 31, 2018. 8.B approves $107,567.40 of furniture through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program for three spaces — Larson's Maker Space at $29,035.32, Larson's Multi-Use Area at $33,995.17 and Smith's Media Center at $44,536.91 — from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. 8.C awards BID 9843, sound system replacement for the Athens and Troy High gymnasiums and outdoor stadiums, to Hardy & Son's Sign Service at $129,297.64 from the General Fund and Student Activity Fund; the tabulation shows Hardy at $64,648.82 per school against Sound Planning Communications at $173,866.60 and Sound Engineering at $188,318.00 in total.

**What the June minutes record**
The June 20 meeting opened with the public hearing on the 2017-2018 proposed budget, presented by Mr. West and closed at 7:15 p.m. with no questions from board members or the audience. The Board then ratified the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA agreement reached June 9, 2017 for July 1, 2017 through January 31, 2020; appointed David Recker as Assistant Principal at Larson; adopted World Language materials for grades 6-12 at $419,606.82 and ELD materials at $171,735.32; amended the 2016-17 budget, with the General Fund at $146,020,168; and adopted the 2017-18 appropriations — General Fund $147,430,144, Special Revenue $9,516,614, Debt Service $18,778,792, 2014 Capital Project $21,615,000 and Capital Maintenance $1,270,000 — at millage rates of 18.0000 non-homestead general operating, 11.6320 commercial personal property, 5.6320 homestead, and 4.7000 debt retirement on all properties. It also authorized sale of roughly 18 acres of vacant land north of Long Lake, east of Rochester Road and west of Allison Street to Mondrian Properties, L.L.C. for $4,225,000.00, and approved a transportation services contract with First Student.

The June 20 Mission Moment recognized the Athens AP Seminar and Research program, with Dr. Lara Dixon introducing teachers Brenda Rice, Sue Syme and Rachel Webb and eight students taking questions from the Board for about twenty minutes. Superintendent Machesky then showed a "2016-2017 School Year in Review" video, thanking School Life publisher Raad Alawan and photographer Rodney Curtis. The June 6 and June 13 special meetings and closed sessions dealt with negotiations and the superintendent's evaluation.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, July 18, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. The consent agenda carries six sets of minutes: the June 6, 2017 special meeting and closed session, the June 6, 2017 regular meeting, the June 13, 2017 special meeting and closed session, the June 13, 2017 workshop, the June 20, 2017 special meeting and closed session, and the June 20, 2017 regular meeting.

**Personnel: the superintendent's contract.** Item 6.A records that the Board recently completed Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and wished to share its assessment with the community: he has completed his third year as a HIGHLY EFFECTIVE superintendent and has met or exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories; his vision is described as data-based, collaborative and reinforced with every interaction with all stakeholders; and the Board appreciates his organizational development for himself and his staff. The resolution extends his contract from July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2020, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the provisions of the written Agreement.

Item 6.B approves successor contracts for Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services. Their current contracts expire June 30, 2018; the successor contracts commence July 1, 2017 and terminate June 30, 2019.

Item 6.C extends administrative contracts through June 30, 2019, without tenure and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook where applicable. The list covers Ryan Brinks (Associate Principal, International Academy-East), Lara Dixon (Principal, Athens High School), Remo Roncone (Principal, Troy High School), Joe Duda (Principal, Larson Middle School), Timothy Fulcher (Principal, Smith Middle School), Audra Melton (Principal, Baker Middle School), and the elementary principals Joyce Brasington (Wattles), Janice Brzezinski (Hill), Brian Canfield (Schroeder), Mike Cottone (Troy Union), Tammy DiPonio (Costello), Sarah Glasser (Hamilton), Matt Jansen (Wass), Melanie Morey (Barnard), John Pagel (Martell) and Jeremey Whan (Bemis). Assistant principals extended are Melissa Curth (Troy High), Robert Dowd (Athens), Dan House (Troy High), Dan Mills (Athens), William Turner (Athens), Brian Zawislak (Troy High), Amy Buchanan (Smith), Jonathan Cross (Baker) and Anthony Morse (Boulan Park). The directors are Kerry Birmingham (Communications & Strategic Initiatives), Rob Carson (Maintenance and Operations), Jennifer Gottlieb (Student Growth, Equity & Accountability), Michael Jolly (Athletics, CTE and Enrichment), David Pass (Employee Services), Christin Silagy (ELD, Federal Grants & State Assessments) and Stephanie Trotter (Finance).

**Curriculum: MHSAA membership.** Item 7.A adopts the resolution needed to continue membership in the Michigan High School Athletic Association, a voluntary nonprofit corporation, for August 1, 2017 through July 31, 2018. It enrolls the six secondary schools under the Board's direction as members and to participate in approved interschool athletic activities, delegates supervision and control to the Superintendent or designee, accepts the association's constitution, by-laws, rules, regulations and interpretations as published in the current handbook as minimum standards, agrees to primary enforcement, and commits host and participating schools to follow all tournament policies, procedures and schedules. The authorization may not be revoked during its term.

**Business: the sinking fund ballot proposal.** Item 8.A recites that the district is a Michigan general powers school district operating under the Revised School Code whose elections are governed by the Michigan Election Law, Public Act 116 of 1954; that in order to improve and repair its facilities it is necessary to ask voters to approve a building and site sinking fund tax levy of one mill annually for ten years from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028; that the district wishes to put the proposal to voters at a special school election on November 7, 2017; and that the Michigan Election Law requires ballot language to be certified to the Election Coordinator no later than 4:00 p.m. on the twelfth Tuesday before the election. The resolution approves the proposal as Exhibit A, authorizes the Superintendent or designee to certify it no later than 4:00 p.m. on August 15, 2017, authorizes any and all further action required under the Michigan Election Law, and rescinds conflicting resolutions. Paula Fleming signs as Secretary, certifying that notice of the meeting was given under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

The official ballot text in Exhibit A explains that the proposal, if approved, will allow the district to levy a building and site sinking fund tax whose proceeds will be used to make improvements and repairs to facilities; that under State law expenditure of the proceeds must be audited; and that the proceeds cannot be used for teacher, administrator or employee salaries, maintenance or other operating expenses. The question asks whether the district shall be authorized to levy one mill — $1.00 per $1,000 of taxable valuation — for ten years, from July 1, 2018 through June 30, 2028, to create a building and site sinking fund for the purchase of real estate for sites, the construction or repair of school buildings, school security improvements, or the acquisition or upgrading of technology, and for other purposes to the extent permitted by law. It states the millage would provide estimated revenues of approximately Three Million Seven Hundred Forty-Five Thousand Two Hundred Fifty-Seven ($3,745,257) Dollars during the 2018 calendar year if approved and levied.

A draft November sinking fund timeline follows: April for vendor outreach and gathering materials from other districts; May to enlist building captains and reach previous committee chairs; a June 6 board vote to place the proposal on the ballot; August 1 for petitions filed with county and local clerks; August 15 by 4:00 p.m. for certified ballot wording; a mid-August union meeting; August 21 letters to families; August 24 to prepare and print an absentee mailer; a September 8 School Life kickoff issue featuring the sinking fund; PTO and community organization visits from September 8 to November 3; a September 15 informational mailer; September 23 for absentee ballots to be available; letters to the editor and signs from September 23 to October 2; October 10 as the last day to register; an October 15 sinking fund podcast; October letters to the editor and stories in the Troy Times and Somerset Gazette; an October 16 mailer and principal postcard; and the November 7 election.

**Business: furniture and sound systems.** Item 8.B approves a furniture purchase for Larson Middle School's Maker Space, Larson's Multi-Use Space in the old office area, and Smith Middle School's Media Center, in the amount of $107,567.40, through Workspace Interiors by Office Depot and the Oakland County America Saves Cooperative Purchase Program, as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. Rob Carson's July 12, 2017 memorandum to Rick West records that Katelyn Weaver, Facility Coordinator, led a project team with Workspace Interiors and building administrators and staff, that Workspace Interiors will coordinate delivery, assembly and installation, and that the America Saves program provides competitive bid pricing at no cost to school districts and municipal agencies along with rebate incentives based on annual sales volumes. The project totals are Larson Maker Space $29,035.32, Larson Multi-Use Area $33,995.17 and Smith Media Center $44,536.91, with a separate purchase order for each. The attached design materials specify collaboration tables with power, stools and mobile ottomans, nesting tables, mobile four-leg chairs, soft seating, double-sided curved mobile bookcases and porcelain-on-steel writing surfaces carrying a 50-year warranty.

Item 8.C awards the replacement of indoor and outdoor sound systems for the Athens and Troy High gymnasiums and outdoor stadiums to Hardy & Son's Sign Service in the amount of $129,297.64, as an expenditure of the General Fund and Student Activity Fund. Todd Hensley's July 12, 2017 memorandum records that price quotes exceeded the Michigan Department of Education's competitive bid threshold, so a formal bid was processed; invitations went to seven potential bidders and three responses were received; and after analysis with Athletic Director Mike Jolly, Hardy & Son's was the lowest qualified bidder. The July 13, 2017 tabulation for BID 9843 gives Hardy & Son's Sign Service $64,648.82 for Athens and $64,648.82 for Troy High, a grand total of $129,297.64; Sound Engineering, Inc. $94,159.00 each for a total of $188,318.00; and Sound Planning Communications $86,933.30 each for a total of $173,866.60.

**The attached June minutes.** The June 20 special meeting, called to order by President Philippart at 6:15 p.m. at the Services Building with Gottlieb, Miletti and Schmidt present and Fleming, Hammond and Hauff absent, moved into closed session under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) to discuss an attorney-client privileged matter, reconvening at 6:18 p.m. and adjourning at 6:45 p.m. The separate closed session minutes record Superintendent Machesky and Jordan Harris in attendance and no other business conducted.

The June 20 regular meeting began at 7:00 p.m. with the public hearing on the 2017-2018 proposed budget. Mr. West presented the details with a PowerPoint, noting the budget had been reviewed in detail with the Board at the June 13 workshop, and covering tax values, homestead and non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, an increase in student enrollment, and general fund revenues and expenditures. No board members or members of the audience had questions, so Dr. Philippart closed the hearing at 7:15 p.m. Present for the regular meeting were Gottlieb, Miletti and Schmidt with Fleming, Hammond and Hauff not in attendance, along with Superintendent Machesky, administrators Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris, Dixon, Duda, Gottlieb and West, and approximately 60 members of the audience.

The Mission Moment recognized the Athens AP Seminar and Research Program. Dr. Lara Dixon introduced AP Seminar teachers Brenda Rice and Sue Syme and AP Research teacher Rachel Webb, who described how the AP Capstone Program began and evolved. Six AP Capstone Seminar students — Rija Awan, Nathan Babcock, Saihaj Deol, Rishita Gudeti and Nina Popovski — and three Research students — Blake Martin, Pedro Pascotto and Brendt Stephens — attended and took questions from board members for about twenty minutes before receiving certificates of recognition. Superintendent Machesky then shared a "2016-2017 School Year in Review" video and thanked Raad Alawan, publisher of School Life, and Rodney Curtis, School Life photographer.

Resolution 17-053 approved the Treasurer's Report for April and May 2017. Resolution 17-054 ratified and adopted the tentative agreement reached June 9, 2017 between the Board and the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2017 through January 31, 2020; Mr. Schmidt thanked those who worked on it knowing sacrifices had to be made, and Dr. Philippart asked about interest-based bargaining, with Mr. Harris explaining it was the second year the district had used the approach, in which an outside facilitator works with employee and management groups to develop procedures with mutual interests in mind. Resolution 17-055 issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. David Recker as Assistant Principal, Larson Middle School, effective July 1, 2017.

On curriculum, Mark Dziatczak and Jennifer Gottlieb reported on materials the Board had reviewed; resolution 17-056 approved World Language materials for grades 6-12 in the amount of $419,606.82 for 2017-2018, and 17-057 approved ELD materials for grades 6-12 in the amount of $171,735.32.

On business, resolution 17-058 amended the 2016-17 general appropriations and budget: General Fund $146,020,168; Food Service Fund $4,032,399; Troy Career Center Fund $2,215,068; Adult Education/Community Service Fund $3,525,964; Facility Rental Fund $1,000; Debt Service Funds $15,767,323; Capital Projects Fund $16,288,758; and Capital Maintenance Fund $1,885,000. Resolution 17-059 approved the 2017-18 general appropriations, budget and millage rates: General Fund $147,430,144; Special Revenue Funds $9,516,614; Debt Service funds $18,778,792; 2014 Capital Project Funds $21,615,000; and Capital Maintenance Funds $1,270,000 — with 18.0000 mills on non-homestead property for general operating, 11.6320 mills on commercial personal property, 5.6320 mills on homestead property, and 4.7000 mills on all properties for debt retirement. Resolution 17-060 addressed the Section 11 purchase agreement: following a Request For Proposals to purchase surplus real property described as 18 +/- acres of vacant land located north of Long Lake, east of Rochester Road and west of Allison Street, Sidwell Numbers 20-11-328-003 and 20-11-401-001, the district received a proposal from Mondrian Properties, L.L.C. to purchase the property for Four Million Two Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand and 00/100 ($4,225,000.00) Dollars, and authorized Dr. Machesky or his designee to negotiate the terms of a final Offer To Purchase after consultation with legal counsel. Resolution 17-061 approved a contract for transportation services with First Student. Each of these votes was recorded 4 yes, 0 no, with Fleming, Hammond and Hauff absent.
